title: Paramartha Guru Tale 27 (Português)

full_text:
Six months after their first crossing of the Palar river on their hands and knees, Guru Paramartha and his five disciples had to cross the river once again to attend a naming ceremony.

Remembering their past ordeal, Matti halted at the bank: 'Hold, brothers! We must verify whether the river is sleeping before we risk our lives!'

Madayan nodded with grave scientific authority: 'On our previous journey, we tested the water with a hot firebrand. But fire is an aggressive element that provokes the water to anger! Today, we must use a gentle, peaceful diagnostic instrument: cold charcoal!'

Peedan fetched a piece of black, extinguished wood charcoal from his bag.

'Now,' instructed Madayan, 'place the cold charcoal gently upon the surface of the water. If the river accepts the charcoal in silence without hissing, it is fast asleep; but if it creates ripples, it is plotting mischief!'

Peedan laid the light lump of charcoal upon the gentle current.

The piece of charcoal floated peacefully on the water, drifting downstream without a sound.

'VICTORY!' shouted Madayan. 'The river is in a deep, snoring coma! It did not utter a whisper! Step forward, Master, and cross in peace!'

Guru Paramartha, proud of his disciples' scientific rigor, hoisted his robes above his knees and stepped boldly into the water.

However, during the preceding week, heavy rains in the distant mountain catchment had deepened the river. What had once been knee-deep water was now an eight-foot swirling pool in the main channel!

As the Guru took his fourth stately stride, his feet slipped off the submerged sandbar! He plunged headlong into the deep current with a colossal splash!

'GLUB! GLUB! HELP! I AM DROWNING IN THE SLEEPING RIVER!' gurgled the venerable sage, thrashing his arms and swallowing mouthfuls of muddy water!

Standing on the bank, the five disciples stared in philosophical debate.

Madayan observed: 'Remarkable! The river appears to be having a violent nightmare in its sleep!'

Matti shouted: 'Do not wake it, Master, or it will bite!'

Fortunately, a group of village washermen who were beating clothes on granite slabs heard the commotion. Dropping their laundry, they plunged into the water, caught the sputtering Guru by his beard and waistband, and dragged him onto the sandbar, coughing up water and weeds.

The washerman chief laughed: 'The river was never asleep, old man, but your wits certainly were!'

Sitting on the sand, shivering and coughing, Guru Paramartha reprimanded his disciples: 'Madayan, your cold charcoal test was fundamentally flawed! Charcoal is black, which signifies dark deceit! Next time, we shall test the river with white chalk!'
moral: Repeated reliance on flawed tests deepens the pit of superstition. [PT]
